learning_outcomes.text: Apply acquired knowledge and problem-solving skills in new or unfamiliar environments within broader (or multidisciplinary) contexts related to their field of study.
Communicate their conclusions and the knowledge and ultimate reasons that support them to specialized and non-specialized audiences clearly and unambiguously.
Possess learning skills that allow them to continue studying in a largely self-directed or autonomous manner.
Project, calculate, and design products, processes, facilities, and plants.
Conduct research, development, and innovation in products, processes, and methods.
Knowledge about methods and techniques of industrial transport and handling.
Knows and applies methods and techniques of industrial transport and handling.
Know and correctly interpret the meaning and scope of current applicable standards and instructions.
Know the different types to select the most suitable system based on its working conditions.
Know the functional characteristics of the different industrial transport equipment and systems.
Develop the specifications for a transport system and its components.
Have sufficient criteria to search for and select the appropriate means of transport.
Know the constructive, functional, and operational characteristics of the most widely used machines and installations for internal transport within industries.

teaching_methods: Non-face-to-face teaching activities (if sanitary conditions require)
assessment_rules: The final grade will be weighted with 80% for the theoretical-practical exam and 20% for assignments and projects. To pass the course, a total grade equal to or greater than 5 out of 10 (50%) must be obtained. Additionally, a minimum score of 5 out of 10 in the final theoretical-practical exam is required. If this minimum is not reached in the exam, the course will not be approved, even if the total sum of grades is 5 or more. This evaluation system applies to all ordinary or extraordinary calls.
